advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the redundant emit_cross_session_warning() call in reopen() (transition already emits) or hold the suppress guard across the delegated transition() so reopen warns at most once.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:471: `    emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` then `    return transition(ticket_id, "closed", "open", repo_root=repo_root)`
src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:333: `    emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` inside transition()

src/rebar/_lib_warn.py:50-61: guard sets _EMITTING then `finally: _EMITTING.reset(token)` — the guard is released when emit_cross_session_warning returns, i.e. BEFORE transition() runs, so it cannot dedupe the nested transition emit
ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_cross_session_lib.py has no reopen test (search for 'reopen' returned no matches), so the 'exactly one' invariant is unverified for reopen
advisory.finding: reopen() calls emit_cross_session_warning() and then delegates to transition(), which also calls emit_cross_session_warning() on the same ticket. The re-entrancy guard resets _EMITTING in its own finally block before transition runs, so it does NOT dedupe across the two calls — the detector runs twice (double show_ticket I/O) and, whenever the target still names a holder, two CrossSessionWarnings are emitted for one reopen.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, ...) line in reopen(); transition() already emits for the same ticket.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope CrossSessionWarning suppression to the server's actual request-handling path (e.g. a catch_warnings/context inside tool dispatch) rather than mutating the process-global warnings filter in build_server().
evidence: src/rebar/mcp_server.py:599: `    _warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=_CrossSessionWarning)`

build_server() is invoked ~100 times across tests/ and by the CLI entrypoint (search for 'build_server(' — many tests call it in-process), so the global filter is installed by ordinary construction, not only in a dedicated server process
The filter is unqualified (no message/module scoping) and there is no matching teardown/reset, so it persists for the process lifetime and mutates state shared with rebar library callers
advisory.finding: build_server() installs a process-global, unqualified warnings filter `filterwarnings("ignore", category=CrossSessionWarning)` as a side effect of constructing a server object, and never removes it. Because build_server() is called throughout the codebase/tests in-process, this permanently mutates the global warnings state for the whole process, suppressing CrossSessionWarning for unrelated library callers (and defeating tests that assert emission after any build_server call).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that calls build_server() and invokes a single-ticket tool as a non-holder while recording warnings, asserting no CrossSessionWarning is emitted (named input: build_server() + show_ticket tool on an A-held ticket as sess-B).
evidence: Added lines src/rebar/mcp_server.py:595-599: `_warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=_CrossSessionWarning)`
test_cross_session_mcp.py registers tools via _write_tools()/_read_tools() fake servers and asserts `out.cross_session_warning`, not stdlib warning suppression
search of tests for CrossSessionWarning yields only test_cross_session_lib.py; no MCP test drives build_server() then invokes a single-ticket tool as a non-holder while recording warnings
advisory.finding: The MCP server suppression added in build_server() (a filterwarnings('ignore', category=CrossSessionWarning) call) has no test asserting the stdlib CrossSessionWarning is actually suppressed server-side. The MCP-surface tests (test_cross_session_mcp.py) register tool callables against a fake server and only assert the response FIELD, never that build_server() installs the filter and no stdlib CrossSessionWarning escapes.
scenarios: A regression removing or reordering the filterwarnings call in build_server() would leak stdlib CrossSessionWarning server-side, doubling the MCP advisory; no test would fail
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an MCP test that builds the real server via build_server(), records warnings around a non-holder single-ticket tool call, and asserts zero CrossSessionWarning while the response field still carries the advisory.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert `res.stderr.count(_HOLDER_MSG) == 1` for show/comment/transition cross-session CLI runs (not just link).
evidence: Added lines _execute.py:60-63 wrap detection+dispatch in `with suppress_cross_session_warning():` to prevent doubling the CLI's WARN line
test_cross_session_cli.py:84 `assert _HOLDER_MSG in res.stderr` (presence only) for show; line 106 same for comment
only test_cross_session_cli.py:148 `assert res.stderr.count(_HOLDER_MSG) == 1` (link path)
advisory.finding: The CLI single-advisory (no-doubling) contract is only asserted for `link` (count==1); for the common single-ticket commands (show, comment, transition) the CLI tests assert only substring presence (`_HOLDER_MSG in res.stderr`), so a regression removing the suppress_cross_session_warning() guard for those commands — causing the stdlib CrossSessionWarning to double the CLI's own WARN line on stderr — would not be caught.
scenarios: Removing the suppress guard around _invoke for show/comment/transition would emit both the CLI WARN line and the stdlib CrossSessionWarning to stderr; the substring-presence assertions stay green
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the show/comment/transition CLI cross-session assertions from `in` to `== 1` count, matching test_link_warns_for_primary_endpoint_only.
